Mildly dovish/constructive tone: The FOMC held the funds rate at 2.25–2.50% and stressed “patience” with inflation running below 2%, which is consistent with a Taylor-style reaction function and inflation-forecast targeting (Svensson, 1997a; “Fed resembles behavior of Taylor rule”). Market‑based inflation compensation remaining low and expectations little changed fit term‑structure evidence that macro variables anchor long rates (Ang & Piazzesi, 2003; Rudebusch & Wu, 2008), reinforcing an accommodative tilt rather than near‑term tightening. While “strong” labor markets and “solid” activity are positives, the noted slowing in household spending and business investment tempers the outlook. Net assessment: slightly positive.
